error_message: CORS preflight test expected 'https://javelinfund.ca' but got 'null'
root_cause: happy-dom (vitest default env) strips the Origin header that scripts set per fetch forbidden-header rule, so request.headers.get('origin') returned null; Cloudflare Workers runtime and node/undici do NOT strip it
fix: Added '// @vitest-environment node' docblock to api.test.ts so undici preserves Origin, matching prod Worker behavior

root_cause: pdf-lib was only in decap-oauth-worker/package.json (sub-package). Root vitest imports worker source; CI runs npm ci at repo root only, so the sub-package node_modules is never installed and pdf-lib fails to resolve. Passed locally because a subagent npm-installed it inside the sub-package.
fix: Added pdf-lib to ROOT package.json devDependencies so root npm ci installs it; node resolution walks up to root node_modules. Kept it in the worker package for wrangler deploy.

error_message: POST /api/receipts -> 500 {"ok":false,"error":"internal error"}; live worker log: 'Error: You do not have permission to call DriveApp.getFolderById. Required permissions: (.../auth/drive.readonly || .../auth/drive)'. Every issued receipt ends status=cancelled, driveFileId empty; Download button returns 410.
root_cause: The Apps Script web app was deployed/authorized BEFORE the DriveApp archival code existed, so Google never granted the script the drive OAuth scope. receipt.store calls DriveApp.getFolderById which throws an authorization error. The Worker's generic outer catch masked the real error as 'internal error', and its post-reserve catch called receipt.cancel on every failure -> all serials consumed and cancelled. Cancelled status then made GET /<serial>/pdf return 410 on Download.
fix: PRIMARY (operator, only fix that restores archival): in Apps Script editor run a function that touches DriveApp once and complete the OAuth consent for the drive scope, then redeploy the web app (Manage deployments) so the live deployment carries the new scope. CODE MITIGATIONS shipped: (1) Worker outer catch now returns the real error message (endpoint is admin-only). (2) receipt.store made best-effort -- a Drive failure no longer cancels the serial or 500s; the receipt is still issued (PDF returned, re-download regenerates from the Sheet row), response carries archived:false. Only build/render failures void the serial.

error_message: Apps Script editor: 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'parameter') at doPost (Code:207)'. User ran doPost manually trying to trigger the Drive OAuth consent; consent never appeared no matter which function was run.
root_cause: Two things. (1) doPost(e) is a web-app entry point that reads e.parameter/e.postData; running it from the editor Run button passes no event arg, so e is undefined and e.parameter throws. (2) The Drive consent never fired because the only editor-runnable functions either need an event (doPost) or bail before reaching DriveApp; Apps Script's static scope detection needs an actually-runnable code path that touches DriveApp to prompt. If appsscript.json pins oauthScopes without drive, auto-detection is also overridden.
fix: Added a dedicated zero-arg authorizeDrive() function that calls DriveApp.getFolderById(RECEIPTS_FOLDER_ID).getName() -> forces the consent dialog when run from the editor. Added apps-script/appsscript.json with explicit oauthScopes (spreadsheets, drive, script.external_request) so the drive scope is always requested. Operator: run authorizeDrive (NOT doPost), approve consent, then redeploy the web app to a new version.

error_message: After authorizing Drive, receipt.store STILL fails but with a DIFFERENT error: 'You do not have permission to call DriveApp.Folder.createFile. Required permissions: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive' (previously it failed on getFolderById needing drive.readonly||drive).
root_cause: The first authorizeDrive() only called getFolderById().getName() — a READ. Google's granular consent therefore granted only the read-only Drive scope (drive.readonly). getFolderById now succeeds, but folder.createFile() (writing the archived PDF) requires the full read-WRITE scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive, which a read-only consent does not cover. The error advancing from getFolderById to createFile confirms partial authorization.
fix: Replaced authorizeDrive() with authorizeDriveWrite() which actually creates + trashes a probe file, forcing Google to request the full drive (write) scope. Operator must: (1) ensure appsscript.json oauthScopes lists 'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive' (not .readonly), (2) run authorizeDriveWrite, (3) keep ALL boxes checked on the granular consent screen (do not uncheck Drive), (4) redeploy the web app to a new version.
